intro.quote: A particular PE must be able to determine how to send traffic to MAC addresses that belong to or are behind CEs connected to other PEs, i.e., to remote CEs or hosts behind remote CEs.

steps.explain: The advertising PE uses MP-BGP to send other PEs in the EVPN instance the MAC addresses learned from its locally attached CEs.

cite.quote: This document requires a PE to learn remote MAC addresses in the control plane. In order to achieve this, each PE advertises the MAC addresses it learns from its locally attached CEs in the control plane, to all the other PEs in that EVPN instance, using MP-BGP and, specifically, the MAC/IP Advertisement route.

intro.quote: PEs connected to the same Ethernet segment can automatically discover each other with minimal to no configuration through the exchange of the Ethernet Segment route.

steps.explain: PE1 advertises the Ethernet Segment route to PE2 with the ES-Import extended community.

cite.quote: When a PE discovers the ESI of the attached Ethernet segment, it advertises an Ethernet Segment route with the associated ES-Import extended community attribute.

steps.explain: PE2 also advertises an Ethernet Segment route to PE1 with the ES-Import extended community.

cite.quote: When a PE discovers the ESI of the attached Ethernet segment, it advertises an Ethernet Segment route with the associated ES-Import extended community attribute.

intro.quote: This document defines a new BGP Network Layer Reachability Information (NLRI) called the EVPN NLRI.

fields.name: Route Type
fields.explain: Identifies the EVPN route encoding used for the route-specific payload.

cite.quote: The Route Type field defines the encoding of the rest of the EVPN NLRI (Route Type specific EVPN NLRI).

fields.name: Length
fields.explain: Gives the size in octets of the route-specific EVPN NLRI.

cite.quote: The Length field indicates the length in octets of the Route Type specific field of the EVPN NLRI.

fields.name: Route Type specific
fields.explain: Carries the fields selected by the route type.

cite.quote: The Route Type field defines the encoding of the rest of the EVPN NLRI (Route Type specific EVPN NLRI).

intro.quote: An Ethernet A-D route type specific EVPN NLRI consists of the following:

fields.name: Route Distinguisher (RD)
fields.explain: For the Ethernet A-D per Ethernet Segment route, a Type 1 RD built from the PE address and a number unique on that PE. (The per-EVI A-D route uses the MAC-VRF RD instead.)

cite.quote: The Route Distinguisher (RD) MUST be a Type 1 RD [RFC4364]. The value field comprises an IP address of the PE (typically, the loopback address) followed by a number unique to the PE.

fields.name: Ethernet Segment Identifier
fields.explain: Identifies the Ethernet segment associated with the route.

cite.quote: The Ethernet Segment Identifier MUST be a 10-octet entity as described in Section 5 ("Ethernet Segment").

fields.name: Ethernet Tag ID
fields.explain: Identifies the particular broadcast domain covered by the route.

cite.quote: An Ethernet Tag ID is a 32-bit field containing either a 12-bit or 24-bit identifier that identifies a particular broadcast domain (e.g., a VLAN) in an EVPN instance.

fields.name: MPLS Label
fields.explain: Carries a label while being treated as a route attribute rather than part of the BGP route key.

cite.quote: The MPLS Label field is to be treated as a route attribute as opposed to being part of the route.

intro.quote: A MAC/IP Advertisement route type specific EVPN NLRI consists of the following:

fields.name: RD
fields.explain: Uses the route distinguisher of the advertising PE's MAC-VRF, which is unique across that PE's MAC-VRFs.

cite.quote: The Route Distinguisher (RD) MUST be set to the RD of the MAC-VRF that is advertising the NLRI. An RD MUST be assigned for a given MAC-VRF on a PE. This RD MUST be unique across all MAC-VRFs on a PE.

fields.name: Ethernet Segment Identifier
fields.explain: Carries the 10-octet Ethernet Segment Identifier for the advertisement.

cite.quote: The Ethernet Segment Identifier is set to the 10-octet ESI described in Section 5 ("Ethernet Segment").

fields.name: Ethernet Tag ID
fields.explain: Identifies the broadcast domain in the EVPN instance.

cite.quote: An Ethernet Tag ID is a 32-bit field containing either a 12-bit or 24-bit identifier that identifies a particular broadcast domain (e.g., a VLAN) in an EVPN instance.

fields.name: MAC Address Length
fields.explain: States the MAC address length in bits, which is set to 48.

cite.quote: The MAC Address Length field is in bits, and it is set to 48.

fields.name: MAC Address
fields.explain: Carries the advertised six-octet MAC address.

cite.quote: The encoding of a MAC address MUST be the 6-octet MAC address specified by [802.1Q] and [802.1D-REV].

fields.name: IP Address Length
fields.explain: States the optional IP address length in bits, using 32 or 128.

cite.quote: When an IP address is present, the IP Address Length field is in bits, and it is set to 32 or 128 bits.

fields.name: IP Address
fields.explain: Optionally carries an IP address associated with the MAC address.

cite.quote: The IP Address field in the MAC/IP Advertisement route may optionally carry one of the IP addresses associated with the MAC address.

fields.name: MPLS Label1
fields.explain: Carries a downstream-assigned label associated with the advertised MAC address.

cite.quote: The MPLS Label1 field is encoded as 3 octets, where the high-order 20 bits contain the label value. The MPLS Label1 MUST be downstream assigned, and it is associated with the MAC address being advertised by the advertising PE.

fields.name: MPLS Label2
fields.explain: Optional second label: absent, or 3 octets (24 bits) when present, with the label value in the high-order 20 bits.

cite.quote: The MPLS Label2 field is an optional field. If it is present, then it is encoded as 3 octets, where the high-order 20 bits contain the label value.

intro.quote: An Ethernet Segment route type specific EVPN NLRI consists of the following:

fields.name: RD
fields.explain: Uses a type 1 route distinguisher whose value identifies the advertising PE and is unique on that PE.

cite.quote: The Route Distinguisher (RD) MUST be a Type 1 RD [RFC4364]. The value field comprises an IP address of the PE (typically, the loopback address) followed by a number unique to the PE.

fields.name: Ethernet Segment Identifier
fields.explain: Carries the 10-octet Ethernet Segment Identifier for the route.

cite.quote: The Ethernet Segment Identifier (ESI) MUST be set to the 10-octet value described in Section 5.

fields.name: IP Address Length
fields.explain: Reports the originating address length in bits and is part of the BGP route key.

cite.quote: The IP address length is in bits. For the purpose of BGP route key processing, only the Ethernet Segment ID, IP Address Length, and Originating Router's IP Address fields are considered to be part of the prefix in the NLRI.

fields.name: Originating Router's IP Address
fields.explain: Identifies the PE that originated the route and is part of the BGP route key.

cite.quote: The IP address length is in bits. For the purpose of BGP route key processing, only the Ethernet Segment ID, IP Address Length, and Originating Router's IP Address fields are considered to be part of the prefix in the NLRI.
